Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

watch out! interjection

also look out, careful!, mind!, beware, beware of the dog, hey you, watch out!, keep your eyes open, look around you, look about you

classical

Petr. 29.1: CAVĒ CANEM
Plaut. Most. 324b: Cavē nē cadās, astā.
Traupman 312

Cavē!

imperative of caveō: alone; with an accusative (cavē canem); with nē and the subjunctive, or the bare subjunctive (cavē cadās); plural cavēte

watch out! mind!

In comedy often with sīs (“mind, will you”). In Plautus’ verse the final vowel is often shortened in speech (cave); the word is cavē.

Other words

  • Cavē tibi! — look out for yourself! mind out!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 584: cavē sīs tibi; Plaut. Bacch. 1033

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

  • Cavētō! — beware! (a warning that stands)

    future imperative of caveō · also used · classical · Hor. S. 1.4.85: hic niger est, hunc tū, Rōmāne, cavētō

    The future imperative of rules and warnings that hold from now on.

  • Circumspice! — look around (you)! keep your eyes open!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 2.2.41: circumspice dum, numquis est sermōnem nostrum quī aucupet (Lewis & Short s.v. circumspiciō); Plaut. Trin. 1.2.109: circumspice dum tē, nē quis adsit arbiter (Lewis & Short)

    To look about one, see whether anyone is near; with tē, look about you.

  • Cavē circumspiciās! — given for “keep your eyes open”

    avoid · modern · Traupman 97; Traupman 312

    Cavē with a bare subjunctive forbids (cavē quisquam floccī fēcerit, Plaut. Men. 5.7.5, Lewis & Short s.v. caveō), so this says “don’t look around”. Say Circumspice! or Cavē!.

Examples

  • canis ingēns, catēnā vīnctus, in pariete erat pictus superque quadrātā litterā scrīptum CAVĒ CANEM

    a huge dog on a chain was painted on the wall, and above it in capitals BEWARE OF THE DOGPetr. 29.1

  • Cavē nē cadās, astā.

    Careful you don’t fall; stand still.Plaut. Most. 324b

  • Cavē sīs malam rem.

    Mind you don’t get into trouble.Plaut. Asin. 43

  • hic niger est, hunc tū, Rōmāne, cavētō

    he is a black heart: Roman, beware of himHor. S. 1.4.85

  • Heus tū, cavē!

    Hey you, watch out!Traupman 110

See also careful, don’t fall, mind your fingers, take care, stop right there!.
